mechanismModel.identity: phUSD_out(recipient) = amount + floor(amount * exchangeRate / 1e18);  stable_in = amount / 10**(18-decimals);  antimatter_burned = amount
evidence: src/Antimatter.sol:254-256 — stable pulled is a pure decimal rescale of `amount`, rate-INDEPENDENT, and reverts rather than rounds.
src/Antimatter.sol:227 -> lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:212,255 — stable leg = (amount * exchangeRate) / 1e18, rounded DOWN (protocol-favouring).
src/Antimatter.sol:236 — antimatter leg = exactly `amount`, minted by Antimatter out of nothing.
src/Antimatter.sol:215 — the only consideration for the antimatter leg is the burn of `amount` antimatter.

roundingChecklist.verdict: CLEAN. Single truncation (PhusdStableMinter.sol:255, integer div by 1e18) rounds DOWN on what the user receives — protocol-favouring. toStableAmount refuses to round at all: src/Antimatter.sol:256 reverts AmountNotRepresentable rather than burning antimatter the stable half cannot match, so there is no favourable-rounding leg to compose against. Round-trip is not applicable: annihilation is one-way (no reverse function exists anywhere), so no deposit-then-withdraw loop can be constructed. No symmetric/banker's rounding anywhere.
roundingChecklist.confidence: verified against source, not merely inherited from the profile

phUSDRedemptionPath.answer: NONE EXISTS, anywhere in the protocol.
phUSDRedemptionPath.evidence: FlaxToken (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol) exposes mint(:58) and an allowance-based burn(:77) and nothing else. A grep for redeem/burn against phUSD across every top-level sibling (phlimbo-ea, stable-staker, stable-yield-accumulator, yield-claim-nft, reflax-yield-vault, phoenix-nft-staking) returns only voluntary supply-cut burns (yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:448 burns half the phUSD it buys) and interface declarations. No contract converts phUSD back into the deposited stablecoin.
phUSDRedemptionPath.whyItMatters: There is no on-chain insolvency event and no bank-run surface: under-backing can never brick Antimatter or the minter. The harm is entirely on the market/peg side. Any severity claim that implies a redemption failure would be wrong; the findings below are framed as peg dilution and POL drain instead.

backingRatioModel.setup: Let C = protocol-owned stablecoin backing phUSD (held as strategy principal by PhusdStableMinter), S = phUSD supply, r = C/S.
backingRatioModel.perAnnihilation: C -> C + amount (in 18-dec terms), S -> S + amount*(1 + rate/1e18). At rate = 1e18: C+a and S+2a.
backingRatioModel.result: r' = (C + a) / (S + 2a). r' < r for all a > 0 whenever r > 0.5. Every annihilation at the intended 1:1 rate STRICTLY LOWERS the system backing ratio until it converges to 0.5 from above. At r = 0.5 the mechanism is ratio-neutral; below 0.5 it is accretive.
backingRatioModel.worked: C = S = 100,000,000e18 (r = 1.00). 10,000,000 antimatter annihilated against 10,000,000 USDC: C = 110,000,000, S = 120,000,000, r = 0.9167. Repeat with the same 10% slug six more times: r = 0.79, 0.72, 0.67, 0.64, 0.61, 0.59. The floor is 0.5, reached asymptotically.

answersToTaskQuestions.q1_whatBoundsUnbackedIssuance: NOTHING on-chain. Antimatter.mint (src/Antimatter.sol:179-181) is `_mint(to, amount)` behind onlyApprovedMinters, with no supply cap, no per-period cap, no schedule, no vesting, and no linkage of any kind to protocol yield, collateral, or phUSD supply. The approved-minter set is unbounded (src/Antimatter.sol:151). No contract in antimatter or in any top-level sibling tracks a backing ratio, an unbacked-phUSD counter, or a solvency invariant (grep for backingRatio|collateralRatio|totalBacking|solvenc across phlimbo-ea/src, stable-staker/src, yield-claim-nft/src, reflax-yield-vault/src returns only two comments inside ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy about a per-strategy share-vs-principal invariant, which is a strategy-level property and says nothing about phUSD issuance). The sole control is off-chain owner discipline. Antimatter.totalSupply() is the exact outstanding unbacked-phUSD liability, but nothing surfaces or bounds it, and it is not readable in the same place as anything it should be compared against.
answersToTaskQuestions.q2_intendedOrFlaw: The 2x is INTENDED and knowingly designed (src/Antimatter.sol:16-20; test/Annihilation.t.sol:104 explicitly blesses a non-unit rate). It is NOT the opportunity-cost class. The Phoenix prior — rewards funded by yield on protocol-owned capital are marketing spend, not loss — turns on the funding source, and here the funding source is different: no yield, surplus, skim, or pre-funded pot supplies the antimatter leg. src/Antimatter.sol:236 mints new phUSD against zero incoming value, so the value handed to the annihilator comes out of the backing ratio of the existing phUSD float and, when they sell, out of protocol-owned liquidity. That is dilution of other holders' claim, not misallocation of yield the protocol already earned. Verdict: the MECHANISM is intended; the ABSENCE OF ANY BOUND, ACCOUNTING OR VIEW on the resulting liability is not covered by that intent and is what ECON-001 files.
answersToTaskQuestions.q3_exchangeRateCoupling: See ECON-003. There is no rate at which annihilation becomes a NEW drain — it is drain-shaped at every rate, because the antimatter leg is unbacked at every rate. What the rate does is fix the multiplier: total issuance per unit of stablecoin taken in is (1 + rate/1e18), so it has a hard FLOOR of 1x that the owner's only continuous lever cannot reach below. Rate > 1e18 amplifies above 2x with zero extra collateral. Rate low enough to floor the stable leg to zero hard-reverts the whole annihilation (ECON-006).
answersToTaskQuestions.q4_maxMintPerDayBypass: Confirmed and graded as a Law-3 footgun at Medium — see ECON-002. Safe-config guidance included.
answersToTaskQuestions.q5_arbitrageMEV: See ECON-001 -> profitableLoop. There is no atomic/flash-loanable loop (annihilation is one-way and requires real stablecoin), and there is no MEV sandwich surface (no slippage-bearing swap in the path, no oracle read). The profitable loop is slow and permissionless: acquire antimatter free as a staking reward, pair with $1 of stablecoin, receive ~2 phUSD, sell into protocol-owned liquidity. It is profitable for the annihilator whenever phUSD trades above $0.50.
answersToTaskQuestions.q6_yieldStrategyCrediting: See ECON-004. Diff-only claim: the minter pin is CURRENT, but the DEPLOYED yield-strategy/vault version is unknown (nested vault pin 043ff2c is 11 commits behind vault master 0110ce4). Flagged with an explicit re-verification requirement against the DEPLOYED strategy rather than asserted as live.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium: 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'. NOT High: no assets are stolen from a specific victim by a specific attack path, there is no redemption to fail, the mechanism cannot brick any contract, and the multiplier itself is documented intent. NOT Low: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded, and lands on parties (phUSD holders, protocol-owned liquidity) who never consented to it, and no on-chain control or even observation of it exists. Escalation trigger: if antimatter emission is ever wired to a permissionless or high-volume minter (setApprovedMinter, src/Antimatter.sol:151), re-weigh as High.
findings.description: Half of every annihilation's phUSD output is minted against no incoming value, and the standing liability that represents is unbounded, unscheduled, and unrecorded. src/Antimatter.sol:236 mints exactly `amount` phUSD to a caller-chosen recipient; the only consideration is the burn at :215 of `amount` antimatter, which itself was minted for free at :180. Antimatter.mint has no cap, no schedule and no tie to yield or collateral, and no contract anywhere in the protocol tracks the resulting unbacked supply. The 2x emission is documented intent (src/Antimatter.sol:16-20); the absence of any bound, accounting, or view on the liability is not.

documentationVsImplementation.docQuote: src/Antimatter.sol:16-18 — 'Antimatter is handed out as a staking reward across the protocol. Held on its own it is inert; brought together with an equal quantity of a supported stablecoin it annihilates, and the pair is emitted as phUSD — twice the quantity, since both halves are redeemed.'
documentationVsImplementation.actual: Only ONE half is a redemption. The stablecoin half redeems a real asset the user supplied (src/Antimatter.sol:222 -> PhusdStableMinter.sol:226,229 into the yield strategy). The antimatter half redeems nothing: antimatter is not a claim ticket issued against previously deposited collateral, it is free supply created at src/Antimatter.sol:180. The word 'redeemed' imports a backing that does not exist.
documentationVsImplementation.discrepancy: The NatSpec's economic justification for the 2x is false as stated, and it is the only artefact in the repo that justifies it (no story is resolvable — see provenanceAndScope.law2Status). A reader calibrating emission policy from this comment would conclude the second leg is collateralised.

findings.economicImpact: Each outstanding antimatter token is a permanent, exercisable, $1-denominated call on the phUSD collateral pool. Antimatter's fair value is max(0, 2p - 1) where p is phUSD's market price; at p = $1 an antimatter token is worth $1, so emitting N antimatter is economically identical to writing an $N cheque against phUSD's backing. Because phUSD has no redemption path (see mechanismModel.phUSDRedemptionPath) this never becomes an on-chain insolvency; it becomes peg pressure, and the concrete cash loss lands on whatever protocol-owned liquidity absorbs the annihilator's sell order.

steps: 1. Stake in any Phoenix product that pays antimatter. Receive N antimatter at zero token cost (src/Antimatter.sol:180).
2. Acquire N (rescaled) stablecoin at ~$1 — real capital, not free.
3. Call annihilateFrom(stable, self, self, N). Burn N antimatter, surrender $N of stablecoin, receive ~2N phUSD (src/Antimatter.sol:236-237).
4. Sell the 2N phUSD into protocol-owned liquidity (e.g. the UniV2 phUSD pools built by yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol) at price p.
5. Net = 2Np - N. Profitable for all p > 0.5.
profitableLoop.profitability: At p = $1.00, profit = $1 per antimatter, on $1 of deployed capital — a 100% return per cycle, capital-recycling, permissionless, no flash loan needed and no gas-sensitive dust involved. The loop remains profitable all the way down to p = $0.50, which is precisely the backing-ratio floor derived in mechanismModel.backingRatioModel. The mechanism therefore keeps paying arbitrageurs to push phUSD toward half peg and stops only there.
profitableLoop.notAnAtomicAttack: There is no flash-loan or single-block variant: annihilation is one-way (no reverse function exists in any contract), so the attacker must actually hold antimatter and actually part with stablecoin. This is why it is graded Medium rather than High.

findings.attackScenario: Not an attack — an intended user action whose aggregate effect is uncontrolled. With C = S = 100M phUSD (r = 1.00) and 10M antimatter annihilated: C = 110M, S = 120M, r = 0.917. Seven such rounds take r to 0.59. Nothing on-chain slows, meters, or reports any of it; the operator's only signal is the Annihilated event stream (src/Antimatter.sol:239), which reports per-call amounts and never a cumulative unbacked total.
affectedParties: protocol-owned liquidity that absorbs annihilators' sells
the protocol operator, who has no on-chain instrument to observe or bound the liability
recommendation: Treat Antimatter.totalSupply() as the protocol's unbacked-phUSD liability and expose it as such — at minimum a view that reports it next to phUSD.totalSupply().
Bound emission at the source: a supply cap or a per-period mint budget on src/Antimatter.sol:179, so the liability cannot be enlarged by a single call from any approved minter.

If the intended policy is that antimatter emission is budgeted against realised protocol yield, enforce that on-chain rather than by convention — the current code has no representation of that policy at all.
Correct the NatSpec at src/Antimatter.sol:18: only the stablecoin half is a redemption.
findings.mightBeIntentional: The 2x multiplier: YES, explicitly. The unbounded/unaccounted liability: no evidence either way — no story is resolvable for this project, and the in-source NatSpec is the only intent artefact, which carries no suppression authority.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium: the protocol's own issuance circuit breaker permits exactly twice the issuance it is configured for. Law-3 footgun — the surprise test is passed unambiguously (see footgunTest). Not High: no direct theft, and the breaker still bounds issuance, just at 2x the intended number.
findings.description: PhusdStableMinter's rolling 24h issuance cap is charged only for the stable leg. The cap is evaluated against phUSDAmount inside the minter (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:212-223), which is the amount the MINTER mints. Antimatter's own leg is minted directly against Antimatter's separate FlaxToken authorisation at src/Antimatter.sol:236 and never touches that accounting. An annihilation issues amount*(1 + rate/1e18) phUSD while consuming amount*rate/1e18 of the cap. At the intended 1:1 rate the breaker governs exactly half the phUSD it was configured to govern.
findings.economicImpact: The single instrument the protocol has for rate-limiting phUSD issuance under-counts by exactly the factor 2 on the annihilation path. An operator responding to a depeg by clamping maxMintPerDay to a deliberately tight number gets double the issuance they asked for at the moment they most need the number to be right.
findings.attackScenario: Operator sets maxMintPerDay = 1,000,000e18 for USDC, intending to bound daily phUSD issuance to 1M. Annihilators deposit 1,000,000 USDC over the window: the minter mints 1,000,000 phUSD (cap exactly consumed, further ordinary mints now revert), and Antimatter separately mints another 1,000,000 phUSD at :236. Actual issuance: 2,000,000 phUSD, of which 1,000,000 is unbacked. No revert, no event, no signal that the cap was exceeded — because by the minter's own books it was not.
findings.profitability: Not itself a profit path; it is the safety rail on ECON-001's profit path, and it is loose by 2x.
affectedParties: the operator relying on the cap
phUSD holders during the exact incident the cap exists to contain
findings.footgunTest: A competent, non-malicious operator entering X as a daily phUSD issuance cap WOULD be surprised that 2X is issued. The consequence is non-obvious: it requires knowing that a second contract holds an independent FlaxToken mint authorisation and mints outside the capped path. In scope per Law 3.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Until the code is changed, set maxMintPerDay to HALF the phUSD issuance you intend to permit, for every stablecoin that Antimatter can annihilate — and only while exchangeRate == 1e18. The correct divisor is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18), so it changes the moment the rate is moved (see ECON-003). Do not treat maxMintPerDay as a phUSD-issuance cap; it is a per-stable deposit throttle that happens to be denominated in phUSD.
recommendation: Route the antimatter leg through the capped path, or add an equivalent per-period cap on Antimatter's own mint at src/Antimatter.sol:236.
Failing that, rename and re-document maxMintPerDay as a deposit throttle so no operator reads it as a total-issuance bound.
Note the root-cause line lives in lib/phUSD-stable-minter (out of first-party scope); the fix that IS in first-party scope is a cap on Antimatter's own leg.
findings.corroborates: AM-LOCAL-002 (contract-profiler). Retained at Tier 2 because the impact statement requires the cross-contract issuance model, not just the one line. Dedup should collapse these two, keeping this economic framing.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium, Law-3 footgun. The one continuous knob the operator has over annihilation economics cannot reach the range they will want it in, and moves the effective value of the maxMintPerDay cap as a side effect. Not High: no theft, and rate>1e18 requires an owner action whose direction (more issuance) is obvious even if its magnitude is not.
findings.description: exchangeRate re-prices the stable leg only. The stablecoin actually pulled in is rate-independent (src/Antimatter.sol:254-255 uses decimals alone), and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount` (:236). Total issuance per unit of stablecoin received is therefore (1 + exchangeRate/1e18): a hard FLOOR of 1x that no rate setting can go below, and an unbounded ceiling. Antimatter applies no sanity bound of its own even though it already reads the config struct at :250 and could.
findings.economicImpact: Two distinct operator surprises. (a) THROTTLE FLOOR: the natural response to over-issuance is to lower the rate, but at rate = 0.10e18 the protocol still emits 1.10 phUSD per $1 of stablecoin taken in — still dilutive, and the unbacked component is completely unaffected. There is no rate that makes annihilation backing-neutral; the only lever that stops the dilution is setStablecoinEnabled(false), i.e. a full stop with no intermediate setting. (b) AMPLIFIER: at rate = 1.5e18 the pair emits 2.5 phUSD per $1 received, adding 0.5 phUSD of further unbacked supply per unit on top of the structural 1.0, from a single unbounded, un-timelocked call (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:138-143).
findings.attackScenario: Operator observes phUSD softening and lowers USDC's rate from 1.0e18 to 0.5e18, expecting to halve issuance. Actual: issuance per $1 of USDC falls from 2.00 to 1.50 phUSD (a 25% reduction, not 50%), the backing ratio still declines on every annihilation, and — because the cap is charged on the stable leg only (ECON-002) — the effective maxMintPerDay just silently doubled again, from 2x the entered number to 3x. Two knobs interacting in a direction neither is documented to move.
findings.profitability: The annihilator's loop (ECON-001) stays profitable at any rate whenever p > 1/(1 + rate/1e18); at rate = 0 that is p > $1.00, at rate = 1e18 it is p > $0.50.
findings.footgunTest: Surprise on both counts: that lowering the rate cannot bring issuance to parity, and that changing the rate silently re-scales what maxMintPerDay permits. Neither is documented on either side. In scope per Law 3.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat exchangeRate as an amplitude control on the BACKED leg only, never as an issuance throttle. Keep it at or below 1e18 on every annihilatable stablecoin. Recompute maxMintPerDay as intendedIssuance / (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) on every rate change. To actually stop dilution, use setStablecoinEnabled(false) — there is no partial setting that achieves it.
recommendation: Add a sanity bound in Antimatter itself: it already reads exchangeRate's sibling fields at src/Antimatter.sol:250 and can assert mintedForStable is within tolerance of `amount`, so a fat-fingered or oversized rate fails closed instead of silently doubling issuance.
Alternatively scale the antimatter leg by the same rate at :236, which at least makes the single knob govern the whole output.
findings.corroborates: AM-LOCAL-005 (contract-profiler) — that entry records the local half; this one adds the operator-lever model and the ECON-002 interaction.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium if it holds against deployed code: phUSD is issued for the backed leg against principal that was not fully credited, so even the 'backed' half is over-issued. Held at Medium and not High because it is a DIFF-ONLY claim, unverified against any DEPLOYED strategy (the minter pin is current; the deployed yield-strategy/vault version is unknown, the nested vault pin 043ff2c being 11 commits behind vault master 0110ce4); the shortfall size is unquantified here.
findings.description: The stable leg's phUSD is sized from `amount`, never from what the yield strategy actually credited. PhusdStableMinter.sol:229 makes a bare statement call to IYieldStrategy.deposit and discards its return; phUSDAmount was already computed from `amount` at :212/:255. Antimatter's own post-conditions cannot catch a shortfall: :230 asserts only that the stablecoin LEFT Antimatter, and :232-233 measures a phUSD balance delta and requires it merely to be non-zero, not to be correct. SA-004 flagged the strict `== 0` comparison; this is the substantive residual it points at — the guard catches a zero-mint and is blind to an under-credit.

stalePinCaveat.statement: DIFF-ONLY. This is what the two trees say, not what is deployed.
stalePinCaveat.pinned: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/lib/vault @ 043ff2c — IYieldStrategy.sol:15 declares `function deposit(address,uint256,address) external;` with no return. Against THIS tree the discard is correct and there is no finding.
stalePinCaveat.master: vault master 0110ce4 — `git show master:src/interfaces/IYieldStrategy.sol` line 24 declares `... returns (uint256 creditedPrincipal);`, introduced by stories 043/044/048/049 precisely because conservative ERC4626 crediting can credit LESS than `amount`.
stalePinCaveat.abiImpact: NONE. The selector depends on argument types only, and Solidity ignores surplus returndata, so a master-tree strategy does not brick the call — it silently succeeds while the shortfall goes unrecorded. That silence is what makes this worth filing.
stalePinCaveat.requiredBeforeAction: RE-CHECK INSTRUCTION: read the DEPLOYED yield strategy (resolved from chain, for the stablecoins actually registered) and measure creditedPrincipal vs amount there. DO NOT re-check the phUSD-stable-minter pin - it is already current (d6ed1156 == remote master tip) and would wrongly read as the park being resolved. If the deployed strategy shows 043ff2c-era behaviour (no return / full credit), close as not-applicable; if it credits less than the principal transferred, size the stable leg from the returned value and/or assert mintedForStable against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount).
stalePinCaveat.parkRationaleCorrection: PARK RATIONALE CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (review pass): the earlier rationale - that the phUSD-stable-minter pin is stale - was FACTUALLY WRONG. antimatter pins lib/phUSD-stable-minter at d6ed1156, which IS that repo's remote master tip, so THE MINTER PIN IS CURRENT. The stale layer is one level deeper: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/lib/vault is pinned at 043ff2c while vault's remote master is 0110ce4 (11 commits ahead, incl. stories 043/044/048/049, which introduced deposit() returning creditedPrincipal). What cannot be adjudicated at this commit is therefore WHICH YIELD-STRATEGY / VAULT VERSION IS ACTUALLY DEPLOYED, because the finding depends on the deployed strategy's deposit() return behaviour, not on the minter's version.

findings.economicImpact: If the deployed strategy credits less than `amount`, the backed leg is itself partially unbacked, and the shortfall compounds with ECON-001's structurally unbacked leg. It is silent by construction: no event, no revert, no view records the difference between phUSD issued for the stable leg and principal credited for it.
findings.attackScenario: Not attacker-driven — it is a passive accounting drift. Annihilate 1,000,000 (18-dec) against a stable whose strategy credits 999,000 under conservative convertToAssets rounding: phUSD issued for the stable leg is 1,000,000 (computed from `amount`), principal credited is 999,000, and 1,000 phUSD of the supposedly-backed leg is backed by nothing. Repeated on every deposit through the minter, not just annihilations.
findings.profitability: None to any external party; this is leakage, not extraction.
recommendation: In the minter (out of first-party scope): size phUSDAmount from the returned creditedPrincipal, not from `amount`.

In Antimatter (in scope): replace the `mintedForStable == 0` guard at :233 with an equality assertion against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount), so a short or unexpected mint reverts rather than passing. This also closes AM-LOCAL-004's windfall path in the same edit.
findings.parkedAs: manual-review - requires reading the DEPLOYED strategy. Recall over tidiness: filed rather than dropped, with the diff-only limitation stated in the finding itself. Note the limitation is the unknown DEPLOYED strategy/vault version, NOT a stale minter pin - the minter pin is current.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium: protocol function/availability impacted — ordinary phUSD minting can be denied for a stablecoin for up to 24h by a party who profits from doing so. Not High: no theft, self-resolving each window, and only bites when maxMintPerDay is set non-zero.
findings.description: Annihilation and ordinary phUSD minting share one per-stablecoin daily budget, and the annihilation path extracts strictly more value per unit of budget consumed. PhusdStableMinter.mint (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:203) is the protocol's general phUSD mint entry point for any user depositing a registered stablecoin; Antimatter routes through the identical function at src/Antimatter.sol:227 and charges the same config.mintedToday counter (:222). An ordinary minter gets 1 phUSD per unit of budget; an annihilator gets 2 (ECON-002). Whoever holds antimatter therefore always outbids ordinary minters for the shared budget, and exhausting it is not a cost — it is the most profitable use of it.
findings.economicImpact: Denial of the protocol's ordinary stablecoin->phUSD on-ramp for a given stablecoin, for the remainder of a 24h window, achieved by a party who is paid ~$1 per unit for doing it. Griefing normally costs the griefer; here it pays.
findings.attackScenario: maxMintPerDay = 1,000,000e18 for USDC. At the start of a window an antimatter holder annihilates 1,000,000 AM against 1,000,000 USDC: the minter mints 1,000,000 phUSD (budget fully consumed) and Antimatter mints a further 1,000,000 at :236. The annihilator walks away with 2,000,000 phUSD for $1,000,000 of USDC. Every ordinary user who tries to mint phUSD with USDC for the rest of the window reverts with 'Daily mint limit exceeded'. Repeatable each window; combine with the window-reset semantics at PhusdStableMinter.sol:216-219 (the window restarts on the first mint after expiry, not on a fixed schedule) and the annihilator controls when each window opens by being the first to mint in it.
findings.profitability: Strictly positive: the griefing action is the same action as ECON-001's profit loop. Cost of the DoS = 0; it is a side effect of a profitable trade.
affectedParties: any downstream protocol path that mints phUSD through PhusdStableMinter
recommendation: Give the annihilation path its own budget rather than sharing the ordinary-mint budget, or charge the antimatter leg too (which also fixes ECON-002) so the two paths consume budget proportionally to what they issue.
Note the window-reset semantics mean the first minter in a window sets its start; a fixed epoch boundary would remove the timing control.
findings.assumptionGap: Bites only when maxMintPerDay is non-zero for the stablecoin; registerStablecoin defaults it to 0 = unlimited (PhusdStableMinter.sol:125). If the operator never sets a cap, ECON-005 is inert and ECON-002 is moot — but then there is no issuance rate limit at all, which is ECON-001.

findings.severityRationale: QA/Low: liveness only, no value loss, and the boundary requires an extreme rate. Filed because the failure mode is a hard revert on a knob the operator will reach for expecting a soft reduction.
findings.description: When exchangeRate is low enough that floor(amount * rate / 1e18) truncates to zero, the stable leg mints nothing, mintedForStable is 0, and src/Antimatter.sol:233 reverts PhUSDNotReceived — killing the entire annihilation rather than delivering the (still fully valid) antimatter leg. Setting rate = 0 as a soft 'stop paying the stable half' therefore hard-bricks annihilation for that stablecoin, and near-zero rates brick it only for small amounts, producing an amount-dependent revert with no explanatory error.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore;
if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();
findings.economicImpact: None directly. Operationally: annihilators see PhUSDNotReceived, an error whose name points at the minter failing to deliver rather than at a rate setting, making the misconfiguration hard to diagnose from the revert alone.
findings.attackScenario: Rate set to 0 for USDC intending 'antimatter leg only'. Every annihilateFrom against USDC now reverts. For a 6-decimal stable the smallest representable amount is 1e12 (src/Antimatter.sol:254-256), so any rate below 1e6 also truncates that amount's stable leg to zero — small annihilations revert while large ones succeed.
findings.recommendation: Either document PhUSDNotReceived as also covering 'exchangeRate rounds this amount's stable leg to zero', or bound the rate away from zero at registration/update time. The revert-on-zero itself is the right instinct (it is what catches a non-delivering minter) — the issue is that it doubles as an undiagnosable configuration error.
findings.mightBeIntentional: Plausibly: rate=0 as a per-stable kill switch. But setStablecoinEnabled(false) already exists for that and gives a clear error, so the overlap looks accidental.

findings.severityRationale: QA/Low, Law-3 footgun. An emergency owner action has a large non-obvious side effect on a different token's holders, with no on-chain signal on either side. Not Medium: the action is deliberate and emergency-scoped, and antimatter is a reward token with no purchase price.
findings.description: Antimatter's entire value depends on a mint authorisation held by a third, independent owner, and that authorisation can be revoked wholesale with no per-minter event and no view either contract exposes. FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:88-91) increments mintVersion, which de-authorises Antimatter AND PhusdStableMinter simultaneously (the check is at FlaxToken.sol:65). Every subsequent annihilation reverts at src/Antimatter.sol:236, and every outstanding antimatter token becomes permanently inert. Antimatter exposes no view of its own authorisation status and emits nothing when it lapses.
findings.economicImpact: The protocol's outstanding antimatter obligation — an unbounded quantity per ECON-001 — is extinguishable by one call from a principal who is not antimatter's owner and who may not be reasoning about antimatter at all when they make it. Conversely, restoring phUSD minting after an emergency requires remembering to re-setMinter BOTH contracts; forgetting Antimatter leaves annihilation silently dead while ordinary minting works.
findings.attackScenario: phUSD's owner responds to an unrelated incident with revokeAllMintPrivileges, then re-authorises PhusdStableMinter (the obvious one, since it is the mint on-ramp) and not Antimatter. Ordinary phUSD minting resumes and looks healthy; every annihilateFrom reverts with 'phUSD: caller is not authorized to mint' from inside src/Antimatter.sol:236. Nothing on Antimatter reports the condition, and toStableAmount still returns successfully, so off-chain UIs see a configured, registered, non-paused system.
affectedParties: operators restoring service after an incident
findings.footgunTest: A competent, non-malicious phUSD owner using the documented global kill switch would be surprised that it also voids an unrelated token's entire outstanding claim, and that recovery requires re-authorising two contracts rather than one. In scope per Law 3.
recommendation: Expose a view on Antimatter that reports whether it is currently an authorised, current-version phUSD minter, so the condition is observable without simulating an annihilation.
Document the two-contract re-authorisation requirement in the incident runbook: revokeAllMintPrivileges de-authorises Antimatter and PhusdStableMinter together.
findings.note: STALE PIN: lib/flax-token-v2 @ f5300117 is ~9 months old (2025-11-20) and there is no top-level sibling to cross-read. Diff-only claim about that tree.

explicitlyNotFiled.item: Over-payment of antimatter as a staking reward, framed as value leak
explicitlyNotFiled.reason: The standing Phoenix rule that reward over-payment is opportunity cost was CHECKED and found NOT to apply here (see answersToTaskQuestions.q2), so the rule did not suppress anything — but the finding filed is dilution of the phUSD collateral base (ECON-001), not over-payment of a reward budget. No 'the pot pays too much' finding is filed.

explicitlyNotFiled.item: Rounding exploitation, cross-contract rounding composition, dust attacks
explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Re-verified at source, not inherited. Single truncation, protocol-favouring; toStableAmount reverts rather than rounds; annihilation is one-way so no round-trip exists to compose. See mechanismModel.roundingChecklist.

The annihilation path reads no price oracle, performs no swap, and has no slippage parameter. exchangeRate is a stored owner-set constant, not a market read (PhusdStableMinter.sol:141). Nothing in the path is manipulable within a block, and the value transfer requires real stablecoin the attacker must part with, so no atomic loop closes.

explicitlyNotFiled.item: AM-LOCAL-001 (antimatter allowance is silently also authority over the grantor's stablecoin)
explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Correctly graded local-high by the contract-profiler and fully determined inside Antimatter.sol. Not re-filed at Tier 2 per the tier split. Its economic dimension (the victim's stablecoin funds an annihilation whose ~2x output goes to a caller-chosen recipient) is captured in ECON-005's crowding model; the authorization defect itself belongs to Tier 1.

explicitlyNotFiled.item: Malicious-owner vectors (rate set to extract, unbounded mint to self, rescueERC20 sweep)
explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Law 3 — owner assumed non-malicious. Only the non-obvious consequences of good-faith owner actions are filed (ECON-002 cap arithmetic, ECON-003 lever asymmetry, ECON-006 throttle-to-brick, ECON-007 revocation side effect).
Fail closed (src/Antimatter.sol:230 strict residue equality; :252 UnsupportedDecimals), and a C4 known-invalid class.

parkedForVisibleFollowUp.item: ECON-004 must be re-verified against the DEPLOYED yield strategy before action. Every cross-repo statement in this scan came from antimatter's own nested pins; there is no top-level lib/phUSD-stable-minter or lib/flax-token-v2 sibling in this audit repo to cross-read. PARK RATIONALE CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (review pass): the earlier rationale - that the phUSD-stable-minter pin is stale - was FACTUALLY WRONG. antimatter pins lib/phUSD-stable-minter at d6ed1156, which IS that repo's remote master tip, so THE MINTER PIN IS CURRENT. The stale layer is one level deeper: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/lib/vault is pinned at 043ff2c while vault's remote master is 0110ce4 (11 commits ahead, incl. stories 043/044/048/049, which introduced deposit() returning creditedPrincipal). What cannot be adjudicated at this commit is therefore WHICH YIELD-STRATEGY / VAULT VERSION IS ACTUALLY DEPLOYED, because the finding depends on the deployed strategy's deposit() return behaviour, not on the minter's version.
parkedForVisibleFollowUp.recheckInstruction: RE-CHECK INSTRUCTION: read the DEPLOYED yield strategy (resolved from chain, for the stablecoins actually registered) and measure creditedPrincipal vs amount there. DO NOT re-check the phUSD-stable-minter pin - it is already current (d6ed1156 == remote master tip) and would wrongly read as the park being resolved. If the deployed strategy shows 043ff2c-era behaviour (no return / full credit), close as not-applicable; if it credits less than the principal transferred, size the stable leg from the returned value and/or assert mintedForStable against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount).

parkedForVisibleFollowUp.item: Law-2 story-faithfulness is UNRESOLVABLE for antimatter: registered-projects.json carries storyDir=null (no entry in ~/code/product-owner/registered-project-list.md, re-checked 2026-08-18), and none of the 6 commits carries a [story-NNN] tag. The 2x design's intent therefore rests entirely on in-source NatSpec (src/Antimatter.sol:16-20), which carries no suppression authority and is itself economically inaccurate (ECON-001 documentationVsImplementation). A human must supply the mapping before ECON-001 can be adjudicated as intended-and-accepted rather than unbounded-and-unaccounted.

Antimatter is not yet wired into phoenix-phase-2-staging (grep for 'antimatter' across that submodule's .sol/.ts/.md/.json returns zero hits at this commit). Emission policy — who is added via setApprovedMinter (src/Antimatter.sol:151), at what rate, against what budget — is therefore entirely undecided on-chain and lives wherever staging eventually puts it. ECON-001's severity should be re-weighed at that point: a permissionless or automated antimatter minter converts it from a policy risk into an active drain.

Systemic, cross-repo, UNVERIFIED: yield accruing on the deposited collateral is skimmable OUT of the strategies (skimSurplus, seen in the vault trees and used by the promotion dispatchers), while unbacked phUSD keeps being issued by every annihilation. If skimmed surplus is spent on promotions rather than retained as backing, the backing ratio falls from both ends simultaneously. Not modelled here — it spans repos that are stale pins in this tree — but it is the obvious compounding interaction with ECON-001 and should be modelled once the deployed wiring exists.

assumptionsMade: phUSD's market price is supported by protocol-owned liquidity rather than by any redemption right. Verified negatively: no redemption path exists in any repo (mechanismModel.phUSDRedemptionPath).
Antimatter is distributed free as a staking reward, per src/Antimatter.sol:16. No distribution contract exists yet to confirm the emission rate or the payer.

PhusdStableMinter.mint is the protocol's general phUSD on-ramp used by parties other than Antimatter. It is a permissionless external function with no caller restriction (PhusdStableMinter.sol:203), which is the basis for ECON-005's crowding claim.
